convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to call 'MovingAverage_FN' which is a custom indicator with no known built-in equivalent. Also depends on two external .mqh includes (SmoothAlgorithms.mqh, TradeAlgorithms.mqh) containing custom classes (CXMA, CIsNewBar) and trading functions that must be manually reimplemented in Python.

derived_values.name: Value[0..2]
derived_values.formula: CopyBuffer(MovingAverage_FN, buffer 0, SignalBar, 3) — three consecutive values of the custom FN moving average starting at SignalBar

other_exits: Long closed when short signal detected (Value[1]>Value[2] and Value[0]<Value[1])
Short closed when long signal detected (Value[1]<Value[2] and Value[0]>Value[1])

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MM<0 means fixed lot size equal to abs(MM); MM>0 means deposit fraction

custom_logic_notes: The MovingAverage_FN indicator is a filtered moving average using one of 57 possible FIR filter modes (N4-N60). The smoothing method defaults to JJMA (JMA) with configurable phase parameter (-100 to +100). The entry logic is a MA crossover: Value[1]<Value[2] indicates the MA was rising (bar+2 to bar+1), and Value[0]>Value[1] confirms continued rise — triggering buy. Conversely for sell. The filter_mode enum maps integer 4-60 to filter numbers. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen/SellPositionOpen/BuyPositionClose/SellPositionClose functions with deposit-fraction money management. SignalBar=1 means signals are evaluated on the previously completed bar, not the current forming bar. LoadHistory() call ensures bar data availability. GlobalVariableDel_ cleans up global variables on deinit.
backtest_data_needs: Any symbol H4 730 days with 5-digit pricing
python_conversion_notes: The main challenge is reimplementing the MovingAverage_FN custom indicator. It uses a FIR filter algorithm from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh with 57 filter modes and 10 smoothing methods (SMA, EMA, SMMA, LWMA, JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA). For Python backtesting: (1) Must port the CXMA class and its JJMA/T3/VIDYA/AMA smoothing algorithms from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh, or approximate with standard EMA/SMA if exact replication isn't needed. (2) Must port the FIR filter calculation (filter_mode N4-N60). (3) TradeAlgorithms.mqh functions (BuyPositionOpen, etc.) handle deposit-fraction sizing and can be replaced with standard Python backtest framework position management. (4) Entry logic is simple: 3-bar MA slope comparison — rising slope + current above previous = buy, falling slope + current below previous = sell. (5) Fixed SL=1000 points, TP=2000 points, with opposite-signal close. (6) SignalBar=1 means use prior completed bar for signal, fill at next bar open.
